_meta.about: Recurring claims in main.tex. Each \claim{id}{...} in main.tex is one site; consistency.py flags the other sites when one changes.

anchor-id-stability.statement: Anchor ids, which the discovery tools return and the editing tools accept, are the native w14:paraId (an OOXML attribute stored on each paragraph that persists through ordinary saves) or, for paragraphs without one, a content-derived fallback id that changes when its paragraph's text is edited and shifts when an earlier same-text paragraph is inserted or removed. The benchmark itself used fallback ids for every original-corpus document; the item-5 citation defect is this instability.

anchoredit-subset-scope.statement: AnchorEdit, the treatment tool set, is a bounded subset of Meridian Docs: 11 of its 29 single-target editing tools, out of 78 tools the server registers in all (main, f92d2710). The server's other tools (discovery, audit, render verification, indexing, batch and configuration) are outside this benchmark's scope, and the results are not claimed for the full tool surface.

anchors-pre-resolved-no-discovery.statement: Each trial's target anchor is resolved in advance, at corpus-build time, and given in the prompt to both arms. Neither arm has a structure-discovery tool such as locate_anchor or document_outline, so the benchmark does not measure discovery. The control arm gets the same id but no tool that resolves it, so it must find the identified element in raw XML itself.

arm-tool-surfaces.statement: The control arm gets only the generic Read/Write/Edit/Bash tools and raw XML access, with no purpose-built document-editing tool. The treatment arm has no generic editing or write tools; it is connected to the Meridian Docs server and directed to one bounded forward/inverse tool pair plus Read, and the post-hoc transcript audit (not the tool list) enforces that it used nothing else.

audit-tools-out-of-scope.statement: Meridian Docs' format/style-compliance audit tools (audit_document, audit_equation_style) are outside this benchmark's scope. Whether they help an agent bring a document into compliance with a venue's formatting guidelines is left as future work that the current methodology cannot answer as-is.

backend-choice-no-effect-on-outcome.statement: The LibreOffice-only confirmatory re-run is expected to measure the same thing as the original run, because in an audit of every persisted chain Word COM never succeeded on its own. The audit is observational, so a backend effect on pass rates cannot be fully ruled out without a forced-backend ablation. By construction, a success from either backend counts as a pass.

bib-citation-mechanical-simplicity.statement: Bibliography and citation insertion synthesize no new schema-fragile XML structure: bibliography insertion adds a plain-run paragraph (plus a plain References heading when the document has none), citation insertion adds plain runs or a known-good complex-field idiom within an existing paragraph, both carrying already-resolved metadata. The paper uses this to explain why these families are not render-gated and why the arms tie on them.

bib-citation-parity.statement: At single edit (K=1), the bibliography-entry and inline-citation families show no measurable difference between arms: both arms reach a literal 100%/100% pass rate (parity, with overlapping intervals).

checkpoint-b-central-test.statement: Checkpoint B keep-survival is the respec_cascade design's central, novel test. It asks whether the three already-inserted, untouched targets (bibliography, equation, caption), which the abstract, Results and Conclusion call unrelated, already-correct content, survive RESPEC's two mid-chain edits (a reversal of a different requirement) completely unchanged.

checkpoint-b-leak-p0305.statement: On respec_cascade's Checkpoint B, which tests whether already-inserted, untouched content survives the mid-chain RESPEC reversal, the generic tool's raw XML edits leak into content it was never asked to touch, and the bounded tool's never do. The significant result (p=0.0305) comes from the anchor-set-level comparison over 11 paired chains. The table's Tier 1/2 document-level paired test for this measure (p=0.2305) is underpowered and not significant.

clopper-pearson-at-degenerate-rates.statement: Per-family pass-rate CIs use the percentile bootstrap with 2,000 resamples. At a literal 100% or 0% rate the percentile interval collapses to zero width, so the exact Clopper-Pearson interval is reported instead, marked with a dagger; in the multi-anchor tables every Tier 3 interval at 100% is also Clopper-Pearson. The one exception is Tier 2 (an anchor-weighted per-document mean with no single binomial count), whose degenerate [100, 100] is shown as computed.

com-type-library-cache-defect.statement: One of the fixed defects was a missing Word COM type-library cache. It is a deterministic code defect, not a change to the model, its prompts or the grading.

concurrent-fallback-fix-never-shipped.statement: The concurrent-race fix for the render-verification backends (defect 6) was committed but never merged. Every reported chain, on the original host and in the confirmatory re-run, used the original sequential fallback, where the second backend is tried only after the first fails.

control-never-invokes-verification.statement: In the three write-time-verified families (equation, table-structural, caption), the control arm edits raw XML directly and never goes through the write-time render-verification step, so host contention acting on that step does not affect it.

corpus-preregistration.statement: The primary corpus (and the development slice's document list) were locked in commit 1061e0e (2026-08-30) and the 48-document section-reordering follow-up corpus in e813cd7 (2026-08-31). Note c's development-slice equation control run (2026-09-06) was not itself preregistered.

defect-3-table-recovery.statement: Defect 3's fix makes the harness attempt grading on trials that the outer timeout killed but whose output file changed. That fix recovered two genuinely correct table-structural (table-insertion) chains by re-grading their forward-leg output against their own pre-write backups, not by re-running them. Appendix Note d names this recovery as defect 3.

defect-6-numbered-refs.statement: Defect 6 (def:seq-fallback) is the sequential backend-fallback defect: the two write-time verification backends are tried one after the other, each with a retry-bounded 90s timeout, for a worst case of about 360s, over half the 600s per-trial timeout. The concurrent-race fix was committed but never merged, so every reported chain ran the sequential code. The render-gate text cites it as documenting the fallback as sequential.

defect-8-collateral-check-citation.statement: Item 8 in Section sec:defects (def:respec-grader) is a respec_cascade grader defect: the Phase-1/3 collateral-diff check counted the auto-created References/Bibliography heading as drift on a document with none. It did not involve Checkpoint B's keep-survival check. With item 9 it is one of the two respec_cascade harness defects.

defect-fixes-code-only-grading-unchanged.statement: Every defect fix changed deterministic harness or tooling code, never the language model's prompts or weights. Two fixes changed how the harness applied an unchanged grading criterion: defect 3 (grade a timed-out trial's changed output instead of auto-failing it) and defect 8 (count an auto-created References heading as an expected addition). The paper names these as the closest it comes to conditioning on observed outcomes.

defect-fixes-reverified.statement: Every fix that shipped was independently re-verified against real output data, either by re-running the affected chains/trials or by re-grading output already collected (defect 3 was re-graded, not re-run). The one fix that never shipped (defect 6) was caught by such a re-audit.

defects-all-fixed-status.statement: Fix status of the ten documented defects: nine were fixed and re-verified; defect 6's concurrent-race fix was never merged, so every reported chain ran the sequential backend fallback. The unreliable external test drive is a defect of the original environment, not one of the ten.

defects-disclosed-in-full.statement: Every defect in the defects list is disclosed with its root cause, fix and re-verification, including item 5's two citation-family harness defects, and none is corrected silently. The bibliography tool gap behind bibliography's parity is disclosed in Results.

defects-materially-changed-numbers.statement: Several of the ten reported defects materially (and silently) changed a number that had already been reported, until re-verification caught and corrected them. One example is defect 4: before it, the original render-gate table (Table render-gate) counted 29 network-failure trials in its equation and caption rows as ordinary capability failures, and that item corrected them. This is part of why those render-gate numbers moved substantially over the project.

equation-original-control-unpaired.statement: In the original shared-host results (Table tab:render-gate), Equation's control arm (n=11, the equation-applicable documents of a separate 12-document development-slice corpus) that is not paired with the 26-document corpus the treatment arm used, so no paired significance test is reported for that row. The confirmatory re-run (Table tab:render-gate-clean) runs both arms on the same 26-document corpus, so a paired test is reported for all three families.

external-drive-unreliable.statement: An external drive on the test host, holding all run data, was physically unreliable. It disconnected twice during the project, which Windows disk-layer I/O retry/error events confirm directly rather than by inference. The paper names it alongside shared-host contention as a cause of the original write-time-verification gap. It is Limitations factor Four, which calls it a remaining defect of the original test environment, but it is not one of the ten numbered 'found and fixed' defects in Section sec:defects.

follow-up-corpus-48-preregistered.statement: A separate, independently preregistered 48-document follow-up corpus was built for the section-reordering family, because the original corpus has only 11 applicable documents. It was combined with the original corpus to produce the section-reordering results that are reported.

forest-figure-ci-overlap.statement: In the forest figure, the bibliography and citation comparisons show overlapping arm CIs. Section reorder's CIs still overlap at K=1 (combined corpus) and separate cleanly only at K=4.

forward-inverse-chain-pass.statement: Each single-edit task is a forward edit followed by its own inverse on the same starting document, graded against the document's original state, and a chain (one forward/inverse pair) passes only if both directions pass.

four-rows-two-corpus-stages.statement: Section reorder appears twice among the three families not gated by write-time structural verification, so the single-edit table and the single-edit forest figure each have four rows (four comparisons). The table's two section-reorder rows are the original corpus and the combined corpus at K=1. The figure's two section-reorder rows are K=1 and K=4 on the combined corpus.

fresh-anchor-resolution-mechanism.statement: The proposed cause of the K=4 section-reorder advantage, supported by per-cycle data but not isolated by the design (the arms differ in their whole tool surface): on every call the bounded tool finds its target again by structural id, while the generic-tool agent has to reconstruct or carry forward the original document state from one call to the next, so its errors compound with repetition.

gap-causes-contention-and-drive.statement: The original render-gated gap in Table tab:render-gate is attributed to the original host environment, not to the editing operations: shared-host scheduling contention (not sufficient on its own) together with a physically unreliable external drive. The dedicated-host re-run tests this attribution directly but removes both causes at once, so it does not separate them.

gap-was-deployment-artifact.statement: The original render-gated gap on the shared host was caused by the deployment environment (shared-host scheduling contention plus a physically unreliable external drive), not by a limitation of the bounded editing operations. The confirmatory dedicated-host re-run is what confirms this.

grading-exact-order-vs-order-blind.statement: How paragraph comparisons are graded. The inverse leg passes only when the paragraph list exactly matches, in order, its pre-forward state. respec_cascade's Checkpoint B keep-survival check instead uses an order-blind multiset comparison, adopted before any trial ran, so a section move does not by itself count as drift.

grading-external-from-docx.statement: Grading is done outside the agent, by parsing the persisted output .docx XML after each trial, and never from the agent's (or either arm's) own report of success.

indexing-tools-out-of-scope.statement: Structure-discovery and indexing tools (locate_anchor, document_outline, index_document) are not exercised by this benchmark and are outside its scope. Targets are pre-resolved and supplied to both arms, so the benchmark does not measure how reliable the discovery/indexing tools are.

infra-failure-excluded-from-denominator.statement: If a harness- or infrastructure-level failure unrelated to the task (such as a network error or a process-level subprocess timeout) stops a chain from running or finishing, the chain is dropped from the affected arm's denominator instead of being scored as a failure. Note a's inline-citation timeout is excluded under this rule; Note b's control-arm timeout is scored as a failure because it reflects the arm's own handling of a large document. The 29 certificate-error trials in defect 4 were re-run instead of being counted as capability failures.

k4-design-definition.statement: The K=4 design runs four consecutive forward/inverse (edit-undo) cycles on the same document, rather than a single cycle, to test whether either arm's correctness compounds or decays with repetition.

k4-significant-advantage.statement: When section reorder is run through K=4 repeated edit-undo cycles, the bounded (treatment) tool has a statistically significant advantage over the generic tool: 92.9% vs 66.1% steady-state pass rate, p=0.0015. Several sites also call this the benchmark's one or only significant finding.

k4-the-one-significant-finding.statement: The K=4 section-reorder result (Table tab:k4) is the one significant comparison among the primary six-family benchmark's final results. That scope excludes the superseded original-host Table tab:render-gate (caption p<0.001 there) and the respec_cascade extension, which reports its own significant results.

k4-uses-same-combined-corpus.statement: The K=4 section-reorder result (Table tab:k4) is run on the same combined original + follow-up section-reorder corpus (11+45=56 paired documents, n=56 in both arms) as the K=1 combined row of Table tab:single-edit.

licensed-docops-corpus.statement: The primary 26-document corpus is an audited slice of the public, Apache-2.0 DocOps benchmark, whose documents were written by the DocOps authors for its tasks (not collected from real organizations). The follow-up corpus comes from the public-web docx-corpus pool (per-file licensing unverified); it and the three author-owned documents are not redistributed.

model-scope-sonnet-except-respec-haiku.statement: Every result in the paper uses the claude-sonnet-5 model except the respec_cascade extension. That extension ran on the claude CLI's haiku model alias, chosen for throughput and cost on its larger, metered job count.

multianchor-equation-caption-merged.statement: For equation and caption, the multi-anchor extension's data have been merged into the reported numbers (Section results-multianchor, Table render-gate-multianchor). The merge was done only after the canonical original-corpus source, the confirmatory dedicated-host re-run, was verified to recompute to the published numbers.

multianchor-sr-table-not-merged.statement: The multi-anchor extension's section-reordering data is not merged into any pass rate or significance test the paper reports (only its ICC and effective N are quoted), because section reordering's published combined-corpus number already has an unresolved two-corpus provenance. Table-structural has no multi-anchor extension run at all.

multianchor-three-tiers.statement: The multi-anchor extension's outcomes are never reported as one pooled N under the confirmatory corpus's denominator. They are reported as three separately labeled aggregation tiers: Tier 1 is the unweighted per-document mean (N = document count), Tier 2 is the anchor-count-weighted per-document mean, and Tier 3 is a pooled anchor-level estimate. Tier 3's naive pooled N always appears beside its design-effect/ICC-corrected effective N.

multianchor-tier3-neff.statement: Tier 3 reports the pooled anchor-level estimate with the naive pooled N and, beside it, a design-effect (ICC)-corrected effective N. The ICC is a one-way random-effects intraclass correlation estimated directly from the extension's own outcome data, not assumed.

multianchor-up-to-three-anchors.statement: The multi-anchor extension exists to grow N by resolving up to three additional anchors per document from the corpus's own eligible positions. The Limitations section presents it as aimed at the small section-reordering corpus.

native-ooxml-structures.statement: The equation, table-structural and caption families each insert or build a real native OOXML structure: an m:oMath math object, a w:tbl table with real rows and columns, and a SEQ-field caption. None of them is text formatted to look like that structure.

never-persist-corrupt-document.statement: AnchorEdit's write-time render-verification step, used by the equation, table and caption insertion tools, is atomic. It saves a change only after an independent renderer confirms the document opens, and it restores the original file on any failure, so a saved change from these tools is never a corrupt or unopenable document.

novelty-word-ooxml.statement: Novelty: the tradeoff between bounded and generic tool surfaces is under-characterized for document editing. The closest prior work (SheetCopilot, PPTArena) targets sibling OOXML formats rather than Word directly, and there is no known prior work posing this bounded-versus-generic comparison for Word/OOXML editing.

original-host-two-of-three-depressed.statement: On the original shared, variably-contended host, two of the three render-gated families, equation and caption, had markedly lower treatment pass rates. Table-structural treatment reached 96.2%, statistically indistinguishable from its control, so the verification step's reliability cost was substantial for two of the three, not all three.

paired-permutation-test-2000.statement: Paired arms are compared with a paired sign-flip permutation test using 2,000 resamples.

per-trial-timeout-history.statement: The harness uses one global per-trial subprocess timeout for every family: 300s until 2026-09-07, doubled to 600s that day after a host memory-exhaustion episode (many concurrent sessions on the shared host), and 900s since 2026-09-18, an evidence-informed 1.5x raise. Defect 6 measures its fallback cost against 600s; Notes a and b and the item-5 statistics gap involve the 300s value.

preregistration-status.statement: Preregistration status of the paper's research questions and comparisons. The paper places each analysis in one of three groups: fixed or preregistered before any trial (RQ1's six-family K=1 comparisons and RQ2's K=4 section-reorder depth study); post hoc and not preregistered (RQ3, the diagnosis of the render-gate environment); or a separately preregistered protocol (the respec_cascade extension, preregistered 2026-09-20).

primary-corpus-holdout-status.statement: Holdout status of the primary 26-document DocOps corpus: it was not used to design the tooling's original feature set, but it is not a blind holdout. Several defects were found by watching this corpus's own trial outcomes, fixed in the tooling, and the affected chains re-run or re-graded, so the paper does not claim its numbers estimate performance on documents the tooling has never encountered.

prior-benchmarks-fixed-tool-surface.statement: Prior agent benchmarks (SWE-bench, WebArena, GAIA) each measure whether an agent completes a task under one fixed tool surface. None of them holds the task and model fixed while varying the shape of the tool surface (bounded versus generic) as the manipulated variable. This paper does that for document editing.

render-cost-hypothesis-rejected.statement: The alternative explanation for the render-gated families' gap, that render-verification cost depends on the task (e.g. caption fields forcing a document-wide recalculation), was tested directly and rejected, on two pieces of evidence: a code-level review of the tools' OOXML output, and a controlled, sequential, interleaved timing test of rendering real outputs from all three families that found no meaningful difference.

render-gate-retry-history.statement: Table render-gate's original-host treatment numbers for equation and caption changed during the project. Defect 4 (certificate-verification errors) re-ran 29 trials over several retry rounds: equation went from 4/26 to 12/26 and caption from 1/26 to 2/26, and those trials had previously been counted as capability failures. The render-gate Results section points to defects 3 and 4 for this history.

render-gated-families-slower-vs-no-cost-.statement: The explanation that render or verification cost depends on the task type is rejected by a direct timing test. Rendering completed output files from the equation, table-structural and caption families showed no meaningful difference in render time, so higher render-verify cost does not explain the equation/caption deficit.

render-gated-three-families.statement: Exactly three of the six families (equation, table-structural, caption) have the treatment tool's write-time render-verification gate (render with an independent renderer before persisting, atomic rollback on failure). Bibliography, citation and section reorder have no write-time render verification.

report-both-render-gate-tables.statement: The paper reports both render-gate tables: the original shared-host Table render-gate and the confirmatory dedicated-host Table render-gate-clean. It does not replace one with the other silently. The dedicated-host re-run is the load-bearing, final result for the equation, table-structural and caption families. The original table is kept only as evidence for the host-contention causal claim (the contrast between the two tables), not as a competing final number.

report-every-comparison.statement: The paper reports every comparison its design specifies (all six families at K=1, plus the K=4 depth study), with per-family sample sizes and paired significance tests. It does not pick a favourable subset: the null families, where the arms show no difference, are reported too.

rerun-closed-gap-completely.statement: The dedicated-host confirmatory re-run closed the render-gate gap completely: all three write-time-verified families (equation, table-structural, caption) reached 100% pass on both arms, matching their own controls (p=1.0), so the environment fully explains the original gap. Some sites give a narrower version: the Discussion names only equation and caption, one Results paragraph and the multi-anchor text name caption, and the figure caption says table-structural 'closes the remainder'. These are narrower in scope but do not contradict, because table-structural had no real gap to begin with.

rerun-identical-benchmark-dedicated-host.statement: The confirmatory re-run used the same model, harness and grading code on the primary 26-document corpus, on a dedicated, single-tenant host. Departures from the original run: Linux without Word COM, a non-root account, and equation's control arm now drawn from the primary corpus instead of the original unpaired development-slice corpus.

rerun-is-direct-test.statement: The dedicated-host re-run is a direct test of whether the write-time-verification gap came from the original host environment rather than the editing operations: the falsifiable prediction that removing the original host conditions closes the gap. It also changed the OS, the verification backend and the user account, which Methods discloses; the backend's equivalence rests on an observational audit, not an ablation.

rerun-nonroot-account.statement: On the Linux re-run host, whose default account is root, the CLI refused to bypass its permission checks when run as root, so every trial failed (156 of 156 chains). All of them were re-run under a dedicated non-root account, and only the re-run results are reported.

rerun-verified-live-wall-times.statement: The dedicated-host confirmatory re-run was checked to be a live execution, not cached, uniform or short-circuited. The evidence is that its individual trials showed realistic, varied per-trial wall times and grading output, checked beyond exit status alone.

respec-17-steps-three-phases.statement: A respec_cascade chain has 17 steps in three phases: BUILD (5), RESPEC (2) and SECOND EXPOSURE (10). The whole-chain composite pass (completing the full protocol) requires all three phases to pass.

respec-anchor-set-gap-p0005.statement: In the respec_cascade extension, the anchor-set-level test pools each family's Phase-3 forward/inverse round trip as a separate paired (family, anchor-set) observation, 30 in all. On it, control and treatment differ by 46.7 percentage points (p<0.0005, permutation test). This p-value belongs to the anchor-set-level measure only. It does not apply to chain-level whole-chain completion (83.3% vs 8.3%, Tier-1/2 paired p=0.2305) or to the Checkpoint B keep-survival test (p=0.0305).

respec-anchor-sets-none-excluded.statement: respec_cascade covers 24 chains (3 documents x 4 anchor-sets x 2 arms). All twelve anchor-sets are usable and none is excluded at corpus-build time. A chain that breaks mid-protocol is scored as a whole-chain composite failure. Two chains are dropped from single measures, both disclosed: one from the Checkpoint B keep-survival test (broke before Checkpoint B) and one from the Tier 2/3 composite (no Phase-3 verdict).

respec-chain-completion.statement: On whole-chain completion (Tier 1), the bounded tool finishes the full three-phase, five-family respec_cascade protocol on 83.3% (10/12) of chains and the generic tool on 8.3% (1/12). The chain-level paired test is underpowered and not significant (p=0.2305, shown only in the table). No prose statement of this measure attaches a p-value to it; p<0.0005 belongs to the separate 46.7-point anchor-set-level gap.

respec-control-chains-broke.statement: In respec_cascade, 5 of the 12 control (generic-tool) chains broke mid-protocol and 0 of the 12 treatment chains did. In each broken chain, a raw XML edit corrupted the document badly enough that a later step's package-validity gate refused to continue, so more control chains never reached some families' Phase-3 step. The whole-chain composite scores these frozen chains as failures rather than excluding them. The Phase-3 anchor-set-level comparisons do not include them.

respec-corpus-author-owned-docs.statement: The respec_cascade extension runs on three real, author-owned (personal) documents outside the primary corpus. These are the same three documents already added under the multi-anchor extension, which gives n = 26 original + 3 = 29 for the merged equation/caption results.

respec-five-families-table-dropped.statement: The respec_cascade extension and its K=1 baseline sweep cover five of the paper's six task families: bibliography, citation, section reorder, equation and caption. Table-structural was dropped because the tool manifest the protocol checked lacked insert_table/remove_table; that manifest was a stale separate install, not the harness's server.

respec-generalization-strength.statement: How strongly the preregistered respec_cascade extension supports generalizing the K=4 section-reordering finding: it is evidence, not a closed generalization, along two axes (five of the six task families in one chain, and a mid-chain reversal rather than uniform repetition). It is not evidence of generalization across models, since the model changed at the same time.

respec-harness-defects-8-9.statement: Defects 8 and 9 in the defects section are the two respec_cascade harness defects found during that extension's run. Defect 8: the grader's collateral-diff check miscounted the intended, auto-created References/Bibliography heading as collateral damage. Defect 9: a doc_label 32-character truncation collision merged four anchor-sets' baseline checkpoint directories into one. The respec_cascade Results cite them by label.

respec-k1-baseline.statement: In the respec_cascade extension, each arm's cascade Phase-3 outcome is compared against that same arm's own fresh, isolated K=1 baseline. The baseline is one forward/inverse trial at the identical anchor, run separately for every (document, anchor-set, family, arm) combination.

respec-model-change-interpretation.statement: The respec_cascade extension runs on the claude CLI's haiku alias instead of claude-sonnet-5. This is a disclosed scope limitation: the result is not a same-model replication, and because the model, the family mix and the mid-chain reversal all changed at once, it is not evidence about generalization across models.

respec-preregistered-two-way-generalizat.statement: respec_cascade is a separate, preregistered extension that generalizes the K=4 section-reordering finding in two ways. First, it runs all five task families in one chain instead of repeating a single family. Second, it adds a mid-chain reversal of a structural requirement instead of uniform repetition, a condition the original K-sweep design never included.

respec-same-direction-magnitude.statement: The respec_cascade extension's results point in the same direction as the K=4 section-reorder result: the generic-tool arm's chains break mid-protocol more often and its raw edits leak into untouched content, while the bounded tool's do not. The paper makes no magnitude comparison between the two designs, which use different measures and different models.

respec-tier12-underpowered.statement: The respec_cascade Tier 1/2 paired tests (whole-chain composite, Checkpoint B keep-survival, and the per-family Tier-1 tests) have only N=3 documents and are underpowered. The anchor-set-level paired tests are higher-powered versions of the same comparisons; no formal power analysis was run.

run-chain-reused-unmodified.statement: The respec_cascade K=1 baseline sweep reuses run_paper_s7_benchmark.py's existing run_chain, unchanged except for defect 9's fix to how it derives its checkpoint directory (an 8-character hash suffix for labels over 32 characters); the whole 120-trial baseline was re-run under that fix.

section-reorder-destination-validation.statement: A section-reorder destination must be a heading at the same or a shallower level. The corpus-build picker (resolve_section_reorder_plan) enforces this, and move_section separately rejects destinations inside the moved section at runtime.

section-reorder-icc-open-finding.statement: In section reordering's multi-anchor extension data (preliminary, not merged into any pass rate or test), the treatment arm's intraclass correlation is 1.0, so the naive pooled N of 22 falls to an effective N of 10; the control arm's ICC is 0. Equation's and caption's treatment arms show no such clustering, so the paper reads it as specific to the section-reordering family, and reports it as an open finding.

section-reorder-k1-directional-not-signi.statement: For a single edit (K=1), section reorder leans toward the bounded tool but the difference is not statistically significant: combined corpus 92.9% vs 82.1%, p=0.170, with overlapping 95% CIs. Only at K=4 does it become significant.

section-reorder-original-underpowered.statement: For section reordering, the original (primary) corpus has only 11 applicable documents. That sample is small and underpowered on its own, which is why a follow-up corpus was built for this family and combined in.

sequential-backend-fallback-order.statement: Write-time render verification tries its two renderer backends sequentially, in a fixed fallback order: LibreOffice/soffice first, then Word COM only if the first fails. The concurrent-race fix was never merged, so every reported chain ran with the sequential fallback.

single-edit-no-advantage.statement: At a single edit (K=1), the bounded tool shows no statistically significant advantage over the generic tools. Bibliography and citation are at literal parity. Section reorder shows a directional but non-significant advantage (combined corpus p=0.170). The advantage becomes significant only under repeated edit-undo cycling.

six-task-families.statement: The benchmark reports six task families: bibliography-entry insertion, inline citation insertion, section reordering, equation insertion, table-structural insertion, and caption insertion.

state-drift-generic-degrades.statement: State drift: under repeated edit-undo cycling the generic-tool (control) arm's correctness degrades, consistent with it losing or having to rebuild the original document state across cycles, while the bounded tool shows no such drift. In respec_cascade the direct test of degradation as edits accumulate (control vs its own K=1 baseline) is in the same direction but not significant. The paper calls this its central capability finding.

supplementary-docs-location.statement: Material left out of the paper (the exploratory audit_equation_style formatting-compliance pilot) is published under docs/ in the public repository named in the Artifact availability subsection.

table-structural-close-originally.statement: On the original shared host, table-structural was the one write-time-verified family whose treatment arm was not depressed: 96.2% against its control's 92.3% (paired p=1.0), statistically indistinguishable. Only equation and caption showed a real gap there.

table-tool-pair-vs-manifest.statement: The table-structural family's bounded treatment tool pair is insert_table/remove_table, exposed by the harness's own Meridian Docs server. respec_cascade dropped table-structural because the pair was missing from the tool manifest its protocol checked at corpus-build time, which turned out to be a stale build of a separately installed copy of the server.

task-failure-scored-not-excluded.statement: A chain that fails at the task level is scored as a failure at a fixed denominator and is not excluded. This covers a write-time verification failure under host contention and a respec_cascade chain that stopped mid-protocol at a package-validity gate. Only harness or infrastructure failures are excluded. Disclosed exceptions in respec_cascade: Checkpoint B keep-survival drops one control chain that broke before Checkpoint B, and the Tier 2/3 composite drops one control chain whose Phase-3 grading returned no verdict.

ten-defects-count.statement: Section sec:defects documents ten infrastructure and evaluation-harness defects. Eight are general and two are respec_cascade harness defects (enumerated items 8--9). The enumerated list has nine items because item 5 bundles two defects. At least one other defect mentioned elsewhere, the cascade orchestrator's chain-id collision, is explicitly outside this list.

timeout-900-censored-evidence.statement: The current 900s per-trial timeout rests on evidence from the corpus's recorded wall-clock times. That evidence is right-censored at whichever ceiling was in effect when each trial ran, so the value is not a closed or uncensored derivation. It clears the observed maximum, but nobody has confirmed that it clears the true tail: no validation run with headroom above 900s is reported.

tool-surface-only-manipulated-variable.statement: Within each comparison, the two arms run the same model on the same documents, and both produce a real .docx. The only manipulated variable is the tool surface: the bounded AnchorEdit tools versus generic tools with raw XML access.

verification-confound-reliability-cost.statement: The write-time render-verification step shared by the equation, table-structural and caption treatment tools confounded the original results. Its reliability depends on host conditions: on the shared, contended host it often could not verify a change and so did not save it, which pushed down treatment pass rates. So the original gap came from the environment, not from what the editing operations can do.

section-reorder-combined-corpus-n56.statement: In the combined section-reorder corpus both arms report n=56. One document's control-arm chain never finished within the 300s timeout in six attempts (at K=1 and K=4) while its treatment chain passed; it is scored as a failure, the one timeout the exclusion rule treats as the arm's own task failure (Note b).
